title: Errors in Measurement
shortDescription: Practise finding maximum absolute error, relative error and percentage error with instant feedback.
intro: Use these rules: maximum absolute error = half the scale interval; relative error = maximum absolute error ÷ measured value; percentage error = relative error × 100%.
seoTitle: GCSE Errors in Measurement Worksheet: Absolute & Percentage Error | MyTutBuddy
seoDescription: Free interactive GCSE Maths worksheet on errors in measurement. Practise absolute error, relative error and percentage error online with instant feedback.

questions.prompt: Choose words from the box and fill in the blanks.

blanks.text: The maximum _____ error is half of the scale interval.
The smallest division marked on a measuring instrument is called the scale _____.
Dividing the maximum absolute error by the measured value gives the _____ error.
Multiplying the relative error by 100% gives the _____ error.

questions.prompt: A rod is measured as $36$ cm, correct to the nearest cm. Find the maximum absolute error, in cm.
A mass is measured as $4.2$ kg, correct to the nearest $0.1$ kg. Find the maximum absolute error, in kg.
A length is measured as $20$ cm with a maximum absolute error of $0.5$ cm. Find the relative error.
A volume is measured as $50$ mL with a maximum absolute error of $0.5$ mL. Find the percentage error. Give your answer as a number followed by %, e.g. 4%.
A ruler has a scale interval of $0.2$ cm. Find the maximum absolute error of a measurement taken with this ruler, in cm.
True or false: for the same maximum absolute error, a larger measured value gives a smaller percentage error.
